subject: geography
topic: Map reading: contours, relief, gradient and cross-sections

kept.q: On a topographical map, a contour line is best described as a line that joins places of equal...
kept.explanation: A contour line links points on the map that have the same elevation above sea level. It is the standard way maps show relief without using pictures or shading.
kept.pidgin: Contour line na line wey join places wey get the same height from sea level. Na so maps dey show relief without picture or shading.

kept.q: On a topographical map, contour lines that are drawn very close together (tightly packed) within a small area indicate that the land in that area has a...
kept.explanation: When contour lines are packed close together, it means height changes quickly over a short horizontal distance, which is the definition of a steep slope. Widely spaced contours would instead show a gentle slope.
kept.pidgin: When contour lines close well-well for short distance, e mean say height dey change fast-fast, na so steep slope be. If contour lines dey far apart, na gentle slope.

kept.q: On a map drawn to a scale of 1:50,000, two points A and B are 6 cm apart. Point A is 150 m above sea level and point B is 450 m above sea level. What is the gradient between A and B, expressed as 1 in n?
kept.explanation: Ground distance = 6 cm x 50,000 = 300,000 cm = 3000 m. Vertical interval = 450 - 150 = 300 m. Gradient = ground distance / vertical rise = 3000/300 = 10, so the gradient is 1 in 10.
kept.pidgin: Ground distance = 6 x 50,000 = 300,000 cm = 3000 m. Height wey dem climb = 450 - 150 = 300 m. Gradient = 3000/300 = 10, so na 1 in 10.

kept.q: A map shows a series of contour lines with the following successive values written on them: 100 m, 150 m, 200 m, 250 m. What is the contour interval used on this map?
kept.explanation: The contour interval is the constant difference in height between one contour line and the next. Here, 150 - 100 = 50 m, and this same gap (200-150, 250-200) is maintained throughout, so the interval is 50 m.
kept.pidgin: Contour interval na the constant height gap between one contour line and the next one. 150 - 100 = 50 m, and the gap stay the same throughout, so the interval na 50 m.

kept.q: On a map, a group of contour lines form several concentric (nested) circles, one inside the other. The outermost circle is labelled 200 m and the value increases steadily to 400 m on the innermost circle. This pattern most likely represents...
kept.explanation: When contour values increase from the outside towards the centre of concentric circles, it shows the land is rising towards a high point in the middle, which is typical of a hill. A depression would show the opposite pattern, with values decreasing inward.
kept.pidgin: When the contour numbers dey increase from outside go inside for nested circles, e mean say the land dey rise go up for the middle, na so hill be. If na depression, the numbers for inside go dey smaller.

kept.q: On a topographical map, contour lines are seen bending sharply to form a V-shape. The pointed tip of each V points towards the higher contour values (uphill), and a blue stream line runs through the point of the V. This feature most likely represents...
kept.explanation: When contours bend into a V that points towards higher ground and a stream flows through the bend, the land is cut by water flowing downhill, which is the classic sign of a river valley. A spur or ridge would instead show the V pointing towards lower ground (downhill).
kept.pidgin: When contour dey bend like V wey dey point go higher ground, and river dey pass through the bend, na river valley be that, because water dey cut through as e dey flow down. Spur or ridge go show V wey dey point go lower ground instead.

kept.q: A map has a scale of 1:20,000. Two points, P and Q, are 5 cm apart on the map. P is 550 m above sea level while Q is 350 m above sea level. Calculate the gradient between P and Q, expressed as 1 in n.
kept.explanation: Ground distance = 5 cm x 20,000 = 100,000 cm = 1000 m. Vertical interval = 550 - 350 = 200 m. Gradient = 1000/200 = 5, so the gradient is 1 in 5, which is a fairly steep slope.
kept.pidgin: Ground distance = 5 x 20,000 = 100,000 cm = 1000 m. Height difference = 550 - 350 = 200 m. Gradient = 1000/200 = 5, so na 1 in 5, e be steep slope small.

q.q: A straight line is drawn across a map, crossing contour lines with the following values in order: 50 m, 100 m, 150 m, 200 m, 150 m, 100 m, 50 m. If a cross-section is drawn along this line, which shape would the profile most likely show?
options: The profile rises steeply then forms a flat plateau at the top
The profile shows a continuous rise without any fall
The profile shows a valley, falling then rising again
The profile rises gradually to a peak at the centre, then falls gradually on the other side, forming a symmetric hill shape
q.explanation: The heights rise steadily from 50 m to a peak of 200 m in the middle, then fall back down steadily to 50 m, in a mirror pattern. This matches a cross-section of a hill that is roughly symmetric in shape, not a plateau or a valley.
q.pidgin: The heights dey rise small small from 50 m reach 200 m for the middle, then e come fall back down to 50 m, like mirror. Na cross-section of hill wey level well like that, e no be plateau or valley.

rejected.why: ambiguous:Contour spacing is unknown; symmetry and steepness cannot be determined.|'gradually' not determinable without contour spacing, but D is clearly best
